strategy.headline: Oakland is the soul, San Francisco the address. Win the Bay from the bridge between them, dressed for fog.
strategy.thesis: Dub Nation lives in two cities. Oakland had the team for 47 seasons until the 2019 move, lost the Raiders and A's too, and still sets the taste. San Francisco and Silicon Valley supply the spend. Curry's next shoe partner is unconfirmed since his Under Armour deal ended, so Nike's sure lane is the team and the Bay's own makers. After a 37-45 season and a 40.5 win total, demand runs on heritage and winter dates: Oct 21 at the Lakers, Cup Fridays, Christmas against Denver. Tell the Bay Bridge story honestly, launch in Oakland first, and pay Black, Latino, Chinese and Filipino-American creators with credit and approval rights. Dress fans for 50-degree fog nights instead of selling them another jersey.

archetype.name: The Dynasty Diaspora
archetype.description: Forged in 40 lean Oakland years and spoiled by four titles, this fan base now spreads across The Town, The City and the 408. It's loyal to Curry, Draymond and Kerr more than to any arena, and it misses Oracle in a building that never had Oracle's soul.

pulse.teamMoment: Curry's aging core ran it back. Last season ended at 37-45, with a play-in win over the Clippers and a 111-96 loss at Phoenix. The Warriors chased Giannis and Anthony Davis without landing a deal. They re-signed Porzingis, Horford, Melton and Gary Payton II, added Niang and Brandon Williams, and drafted Yaxel Lendeborg at No. 11. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are recovering from injury.
pulse.sentiment: Grateful and anxious. Fans are invested in the dynasty-era window but expect little: the win total is 40.5, and previews doubt a play-in spot. That mood favors keepsake and heritage buying over hype.

topInsights.title: The logo already picked the Bay Bridge
topInsights.insight: The Warriors' roundel shows the Bay Bridge, the span joining The City to The Town. It opened Nov 12, 1936, turns 90 during Cup group play, and Chase Center sits a short walk from its western approach. The Golden Gate is the tourist bridge to Marin, and its orange next to navy recalls the disliked 1997-2010 era.
topInsights.implication: Make Bay Bridge cable lines, catenaries and paired City/Town lettering the spine of Bay product. Draw them from public geometry, with a credited letterer. Hold Golden Gate orange (#C0362C) to small accents, and never lead with navy and orange.

topInsights.title: Oakland sets the taste, San Francisco pays the bill
topInsights.insight: Hyphy, scraper bikes, turf dancing, Oaklandish and the We Believe memory all come from the East Bay. The Chase Center buyer is premium, tech-paid and based in San Francisco. Oakland reads SF-only product as the work of the team that left.
topInsights.implication: Open every Bay drop in Oakland: an Oakland maker's name on the tag, and an Oakland pop-up (Uptown, Lake Merritt, Fox Theater) before Chase Center and Union Square. Tier one story from accessible East Bay tees to premium Mission Bay pieces.

topInsights.title: Nike's lane is the team, for now
topInsights.insight: Curry's Under Armour partnership ended in late 2025, and Curry Brand is independent. Reports call him a sneaker free agent, with Nike among the interested brands, but none of it is confirmed. That leaves the franchise's most emotional face an open question, while the uniforms (Specter, City, Icon) and team apparel are Nike's for certain.
topInsights.implication: Build the season on team product and franchise stories: Bay Bridge, We Believe, Run TMC, 1975, Strength in Numbers. Until his partner is confirmed, use no Curry likeness, no 'Night Night', no No. 30 hero use and no Curry-linked causes. If he signs with Nike, the dynasty-window story leads. If he signs with a rival, it stays off.

topInsights.title: This is a winter-only year
topInsights.insight: After a play-in exit and with a 40.5 win total, the April-June peak isn't guaranteed. That peak usually carries Warriors retail. The money is in the Oct 21 ESPN game at the Lakers, Cup Fridays from Oct 30 and the Black Friday run. So is Dec 25 against Denver at Chase Center (7:30 p.m. PT), during Dungeness crab season.
topInsights.implication: Front-load existing in-line product into October-December. Treat new Bay-specific pieces this winter as small local pilots, since full Nike development runs many months ahead. Build spring playoff gear as a contingent 48-hour fast-turn, not a committed buy.

topInsights.title: Fog is the product brief
topInsights.insight: Chase Center nights sit in the 50s with wind off the bay, and the season runs through atmospheric-river rain. Locals layer instead of wearing parkas: fleece or a quarter-zip under a light shell, hood up. Hoodies, warm-ups and shells sell most of the year, and shorts get a narrow September-October window.
topInsights.implication: Make a fog-gray layering system the Warriors' everyday best-seller: packable shell, midweight half-zip, vest, beanie, all cut to sit over a jersey. Offer true women's and youth fits. Style it on BART riders and Thrive City crowds, not the tech-vest look locals mock.

topInsights.title: Asian American heritage is core business, not a theme night
topInsights.insight: Asian Americans are more than a third of San Francisco and Santa Clara County. SoMa Pilipinas sits a walk from Chase Center, and Daly City, Chinatown and San Jose's Little Saigon anchor the fan base. The Bay also invented Filipino-American battle turntablism (Invisibl Skratch Piklz).
topInsights.implication: Show up now for Filipino American History Month with paid, credited work and no merchandise. Sign a Chinatown-rooted artist by early November for a small Year of the Goat capsule (Feb 6, 2027). Be open that the full Filipino capsule is an October 2027 build, and skip generic dragons and 'chop suey' type.

topInsights.title: Underdogs and team-first stories beat dynasty hype
topInsights.insight: We Believe turns 20 in spring 2027 and shares a soundtrack with hyphy (E-40's 2006 breakout). Bay vintage dealers and the Alameda Point flea already trade Run TMC, We Believe and Oakland-era gear, and fans buy it before the current jersey. 'Strength in Numbers' suits a roster with few new stars better than star-led gear does.
topInsights.implication: Make heritage the hero category, with numbered, story-led pieces priced as collector items. Use Strength in Numbers as the through-line for team-first product. That keeps new gear from being compared with cheap vintage or tied to one injured player.

partners.name: Marcus Books and the Bayview Opera House
partners.type: Black cultural institutions (Oakland bookstore; Bayview arts center)
partners.why: Marcus Books is the country's oldest Black-owned bookstore and the Bayview Opera House anchors Black San Francisco on the T Third line to Chase Center.
partners.idea: Co-host Black History Month programming and sell the Oakland printmaker capsule, with a fee, revenue share and approval over iconography.

partners.name: Scraper Bike Team
partners.why: It turned Oakland's scraper car style into candy-colored, foil-spoked bikes and a youth program, which makes it the most credible car-culture partner.
partners.idea: Co-design Scraper Spokes and the Scraper Royal pitch. Credit builders on jock tags and fund the youth program as a line item.

partners.name: SoMa Pilipinas
partners.why: It sits a short walk from Chase Center and marks a community South of Market has housed for generations.
partners.idea: Give it this October's no-merchandise support. Then have it co-lead the 2027 Filipino Heritage capsule with Bay Filipino-American DJs and a launch in the district.

partners.name: Chinese Historical Society of America Museum
partners.why: It documents the country's oldest Chinatown and keeps Lunar New Year product specific instead of generic.
partners.idea: Co-curate the Year of the Goat capsule with a Chinatown artist and calligrapher, with an exhibit-linked launch.

partners.name: Precita Eyes Mural Arts & Visitors Center
partners.why: It's the community-accountable way to commission Mission muralists, instead of using murals as a backdrop.
partners.idea: A multi-artist panel jacket for Carnaval and Latino heritage night, with every panel credited and paid.

partners.name: FTC Skateboarding
partners.why: Its multiple Nike SB Dunk collaborations make it San Francisco's most direct sneaker-culture link to Nike.
partners.idea: Host the summer SB royal-and-gold tie-in with a credited San Francisco skate artist, sold through skater-owned shops.

where: Oakland first for identity: Uptown/Broadway, Lake Merritt and Temescal pop-ups, plus Oaklandish and the Fox Theater for launches
Chase Center team shop and Thrive City for game-night volume, Specter restocks and watch parties
Union Square, Valley Fair and Santana Row for holiday, tourist and premium Silicon Valley spend
Shoe Palace, FTC and skater-owned shops for sneaker-first and skate buyers; Gilroy and Livermore factory stores for value entry
Haight vintage, Amoeba and the Mission for archive walls and poster product that earn taste before mass release
when: October-December is the spine: the Oct 21 ESPN game, Cup Fridays from Oct 30, the Nov 12 bridge pilot, Black Friday and Dec 25
Heritage windows: Filipino American History Month now, with no merch, then Lunar New Year (Feb 6, 2027) and Black History Month
Spring is contingent: We Believe 20 ships either way, and playoff gear turns in 48 hours only if the team qualifies
Summer is for layers, skate and scraper bikes; fall 2027 is when the full Bay line ships
how: Pilot this winter at local-print scale and say so. Build the full 2027-28 lines from the pilots' sell-through
Launch in Oakland, then San Francisco, then the South Bay, with a named, paid local maker on every Bay tag
Offer true women's and youth fits in every core piece, not unisex re-labels
Number pieces and pair them with posters so new heritage product beats cheap vintage. Promote with member access and shipping thresholds, not discounts
Sell the team, not Curry: lead with Specter, City and Strength in Numbers until his next partner is confirmed

risks.risk: Oakland backlash: 'The Town' product designed in Portland and sold in Mission Bay reads as appropriation by the team that left. The Raiders and A's left too.
risks.mitigation: Use paid Oakland makers on the tag, Oakland launch venues and money back into Oakland programs. Keep Raiders and A's marks off, and never treat Oakland as a nostalgia prop.

risks.risk: Curry uncertainty: he left Under Armour in late 2025 and his next partner is unconfirmed. Curry-adjacent product or causes could end up promoting a rival, or miss a Nike upside.
risks.mitigation: Keep Curry likeness, No. 30 hero use and Curry-linked causes off until his deal is confirmed. Have a dynasty-window capsule briefed and ready if he signs with Nike.

risks.risk: Lead times: Nike apparel, team and NBA approvals and paid co-design can't hit Nov 12 or Dec 25 as full collections.
risks.mitigation: Ship only pilots this winter: one artist, local screenprint, existing blanks, team-approved. Ask the team now for Specter, City Edition and licensing lead times, and build full lines for 2027-28.

risks.risk: Cultural lifting: hyphy slang, scraper-bike style and lowrider pinstripes come from Black Oakland and Chicano communities, and only some partners are signed.
risks.mitigation: Develop nothing from a community without a named, paid partner from it who holds approval rights. The lowrider half stays on hold until a Chicano-led club or painter signs.

risks.risk: A licensing thicket: the Golden Gate Bridge district, The Bay Lights and SFMTA's Muni worm. It also takes in Fillmore and Grateful Dead archive art, Hieroglyphics and Thizz marks, We Believe and Oracle audio, and mural copyright.
risks.mitigation: Commission original art from living Bay artists, draw bridges from public geometry, and clear every third-party and pre-Oakland mark with the team and NBA before sampling.

scorecard.rationale: Oakland, San Francisco and Asian American lineages put the Bay's design well in the league's top band, and its spending keeps retail high. A 40.5-win total and an open Curry shoe deal hold opportunity and fandom at the league middle (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 70). Culture scores near the top: two cities, three subcultural lineages and huge Asian American communities. Opportunity sits in the low 70s, held down by a 40.5 win total, injured Butler and Moody, an open Curry deal and a winter-only window. A Curry-Nike deal, confirmed Specter game dates and a hot November would push it back toward 80.

music.headline: Hyphy and We Believe are the same memory, and it belongs to The Town.
music.summary: The Bay has invented its sound three times: 1960s Fillmore psychedelia, mid-2000s hyphy out of Vallejo and Oakland, and battle turntablism from Filipino-American DJ crews. The rap canon fans rep is overwhelmingly East Bay. After a 37-45 season, music can keep Dub Nation invested when the standings don't. Make it with the artists who own that sound, and launch it in their rooms.

insights.title: Hyphy and We Believe are one memory
insights.detail: Hyphy, the hyperactive rap and dance movement of Mac Dre, Keak da Sneak, Mistah F.A.B. and E-40, broke nationally with E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go' in 2006. That same window gave Oracle the 2007 We Believe Warriors, an 8 seed that knocked off 67-win Dallas in front of a roaring crowd.
insights.implication: For fans now in their 30s and 40s, hyphy's language and look are the soundtrack of their Warriors. Build an Oakland-heritage capsule from that vocabulary, with Vallejo and Oakland artists, not from a mood board.

insights.title: E-40 is Dub Nation's most visible celebrity fan
insights.detail: The Vallejo rapper has sat courtside since the Oracle years. In the 2023 Warriors-Kings playoff series he was escorted out of Sacramento's Golden 1 Center. He called it racial profiling, and the Bay rallied behind him.
insights.implication: He is the most credible bridge between the team and Bay rap, but he runs his own wine and spirits businesses (Earl Stevens Selections, Sluricane). Approach him as a paid co-creator with clear category boundaries, never as a cameo.

insights.title: The arena sound has a name: DJ D-Sharp
insights.detail: DJ D-Sharp, the Warriors' longtime in-arena DJ, carried the team's mix of Bay slaps and anthems from Oracle Arena to Chase Center. For many fans, the in-game sound is his.
insights.implication: Make him the paid music curator for city drops. A licensed D-Sharp warmup mix as launch content gives product Bay credibility no brand team can manufacture.

insights.title: Fillmore poster art is San Francisco's graphic language
insights.detail: From 1966, Bill Graham's Fillmore posters defined psychedelic design. Wes Wilson, Victor Moscoso, Stanley Mouse and Alton Kelley, and Rick Griffin drew hand-lettered words that swell to fill a shape, in complementary colors that vibrate. The Fillmore still hands sold-out crowds a free commemorative poster. The Warriors have kept the Haight connection alive with recurring Grateful Dead nights.
insights.implication: A numbered game-poster series by living Bay poster artists is the most 'only San Francisco' visual a Warriors product can carry. Commission new work. License archive art from its rights holders instead of tracing the classics.

insights.title: Battle turntablism is Bay-born and Filipino-American
insights.detail: Filipino-American mobile DJ crews in Daly City, San Francisco's Excelsior and the East Bay produced the Invisibl Skratch Piklz (DJ Qbert, Mix Master Mike, Shortkut). Its members won DMC world titles in the early 1990s and turned the turntable into an instrument. Pinole's P-Lo carries that lineage into today's rap production.
insights.implication: Turntable, slipmat and scratch-waveform graphics are earned Bay motifs. They fit Filipino American History Month in October and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night. Co-design the work with Filipino-American DJs, and credit and pay them.

insights.title: Oakland made the music, and felt the move
insights.detail: Chase Center opened in Mission Bay in September 2019 with Metallica and the San Francisco Symphony. The move ended 47 years in Oakland, the city behind most of the Bay rap canon, from Too $hort and Digital Underground to Hieroglyphics. Many Town fans, who also lost the Raiders and A's, still feel it.
insights.implication: Carry both 'The Town' and 'The City' on music-led product, and launch in Oakland rooms such as the Fox Theater. Product that only speaks Chase Center reads as tech-money San Francisco to the fan base's emotional core.

places.name: The Fillmore
places.why: Bill Graham's rock room since 1966, in the old 'Harlem of the West' jazz district. It still gives sold-out crowds a free commemorative poster.

places.name: Fox Theater
places.why: A restored 1928 movie palace where Bay rap and R&B acts play homecoming shows. It's the right Oakland stage for a Town product launch.

places.name: Oakland Arena (formerly Oracle Arena)
places.why: The 'Roaracle,' the Warriors' home for 47 years and the building where We Believe happened. It still hosts concerts and remains a pilgrimage point for Oakland fans.

places.name: Chase Center and Thrive City
places.why: The current home court, opened in 2019 with Metallica and the SF Symphony. Thrive City's plaza is the natural stage for DJ-led launches on game days.

places.name: 924 Gilman Street
places.why: An all-ages, volunteer-run punk club since 1986 that launched Green Day, Operation Ivy and Rancid. It's the East Bay's DIY conscience.

places.name: Amoeba Music
places.why: The Bay's flagship record store, in a former bowling alley a few blocks from the Grateful Dead's old house. The right door for a numbered poster-tee drop.

places.name: SFJAZZ Center
places.why: Billed as the first free-standing U.S. building made for jazz (2013). It carries forward the Fillmore jazz legacy that urban renewal destroyed.

places.name: KPOO 89.5 FM
places.why: A noncommercial community station on air since 1972, playing blues, jazz, gospel and hip-hop for Black San Francisco. A partner with deep roots, not reach.

places.name: 106 KMEL
places.why: For decades the Bay's hip-hop and R&B station, and the dial where Bay rap and hyphy broke to a mass audience.

places.name: Sigmund Stern Grove
places.why: A eucalyptus-ringed natural amphitheater with free Sunday summer concerts since 1938, loved across every Bay demographic.

people.name: E-40
people.role: Vallejo rapper, slang coiner and entrepreneur
people.why: The Warriors' most visible celebrity fan and an architect of mobb music and hyphy. He has the authority to bless or sink a Bay music collab.

people.name: DJ D-Sharp
people.why: He has soundtracked games from Oracle to Chase Center, which makes him the team's built-in music curator.

people.name: MC Hammer
people.role: East Oakland pop-rap superstar and former A's batboy
people.why: A courtside regular through the title years and a living symbol of Oakland's claim on the team.

people.name: Larry June
people.role: San Francisco rapper and independent label owner (The Freeminded Records)
people.why: His wellness-and-vintage-cars persona and his 2023 album with The Alchemist, 'The Great Escape,' make him the city's most respected current voice.

people.name: LaRussell
people.role: Vallejo rapper and independent operator (Good Compenny)
people.why: His backyard shows and fast, fan-owned release model are the new template for Bay independence. He's a natural co-creator if he has no conflicting deals.

people.name: P-Lo
people.role: Filipino-American rapper-producer from Pinole; HBK Gang member
people.why: He links the Bay's Filipino-American DJ lineage to current rap, and he's a credible voice for Filipino Heritage Night.

people.name: DJ Qbert
people.role: San Francisco turntablist; co-founder of the Invisibl Skratch Piklz
people.why: A DMC world champion and the global face of Bay turntablism, who still teaches scratching worldwide.

people.name: Hieroglyphics
people.role: Oakland indie hip-hop collective (Del the Funky Homosapien, Souls of Mischief, Casual, Pep Love, Domino)
people.why: Behind '93 'til Infinity' and the Hiero Day festival, and holders of the third-eye logo, one of hip-hop's best-known collective marks.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's weekend of Latin American and Caribbean music, dance and parade, rooted in the neighborhood that raised Carlos Santana.

moments.name: Fillmore Jazz Festival
moments.why: A free street festival on Fillmore Street that honors the 'Harlem of the West' and pairs naturally with a Fillmore poster-art story.

moments.name: Stern Grove Festival
moments.why: Free summer concerts with an all-ages crowd in the Sunset, an off-season way to keep the brand in front of families.

moments.name: Outside Lands
moments.why: The Bay's biggest ticketed festival, and the summer's peak reach for previewing next season's city product.

moments.name: San Jose Jazz Summer Fest
moments.why: The South Bay's signature music weekend, and a way into a Silicon Valley fan base that rarely sees Bay culture events.

moments.name: Hiero Day
moments.why: Hieroglyphics' Oakland block party gathers East Bay hip-hop heads before the season. It's an ideal place to seed a Town capsule.

moments.name: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass
moments.why: Warren Hellman's free Golden Gate Park festival draws hundreds of thousands just as preseason starts.

moments.name: Filipino American History Month and Warriors Filipino Heritage Night
moments.timing: October (heritage night date set each season)
moments.why: The best moment for a turntablism story co-created with Filipino-American DJs, in one of the country's largest Filipino-American communities.

vocabulary.meaning: Short for hyperactive: the mid-2000s Bay rap, dance and car-culture movement out of Vallejo and Oakland.
To lose yourself dancing. The core hyphy instruction, immortalized by E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go.'
The slow, funk-heavy, bass-driven 1990s Bay rap sound of Vallejo and Oakland (E-40 and The Click, Spice 1, Mac Mall).
Bay slang for a song that hits hard, rooted in trunk-rattling Bay beats and now used nationally.
Oakland and San Francisco, respectively. Every Bay music fan knows which side an artist reps.
The Bay Area ('Yay Area'), a common term in Bay rap lyrics.
The Northern California intensifier ('hella loud'), worn as a badge of Bay identity.
Mac Dre's term, and the name of his Thizz Entertainment label. It refers to ecstasy. Know it, but keep it off product.

designCues.cue: Fillmore melt: hand-drawn letterforms that swell and warp to fill a shape
designCues.source: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters set the template for psychedelic lettering.
designCues.use: Commission Bay letterers to draw 'Dub Nation' or 'The Bay' in this tradition for poster tees and hangtags. Don't copy or trace existing posters.

designCues.cue: Vibration orange set against Warriors Royal
designCues.source: Victor Moscoso's Fillmore-era optical clashes of equal-value complementary colors.
designCues.use: Use it as the single hit color against Warriors Royal (#1D428A) on poster prints, taping or an inside placket, tuned so the two vibrate. The hex is approximate, so match it with a lab dip.

designCues.cue: Scraper-bike candy foil: spokes wrapped in candy wrappers and colored foil tape
designCues.source: East Oakland's scraper-bike youth culture, put on the map by the Trunk Boiz' 2007 'Scraper Bike' video and the Original Scraper Bike Team.
designCues.use: Use iridescent foil-tape piping, spoke-pattern heat transfers and candy-color colorblocking. Co-create with East Oakland scraper builders, and credit and pay them.

designCues.cue: Stunna shades: oversized white-frame sunglasses
designCues.source: The signature accessory of the hyphy era (Mac Dre, Keak da Sneak, E-40's 'Tell Me When to Go' video).
designCues.use: Use them as a graphic icon or styling for an Oakland-heritage capsule, paired with 'Go Dumb' type and never with 'Thizz' imagery.

designCues.cue: Turntable, slipmat and scratch waveform
designCues.source: Bay turntablism, built by Filipino-American DJ crews and the Invisibl Skratch Piklz.
designCues.use: Print the waveform of a commissioned scratch routine by a named Bay DJ down a sleeve. Cut slipmat-shaped hangtags, and credit the DJ on the tag.

designCues.cue: The Roaracle: crowd noise as heritage
designCues.source: Oracle Arena's reputation as the league's loudest building, peaking with the 2007 We Believe run.
designCues.use: Build a Town capsule around decibel-meter graphics and a waveform from licensed Oracle crowd audio in the team archive. Launch it in Oakland.

designCues.cue: Two decks, one bridge
designCues.source: The Bay Bridge in the Warriors logo, combined with the Bay's DJ culture.
designCues.use: Redraw the bridge as the line between two turntables labeled The Town and The City, as the chest graphic for a capsule that unites Oakland and San Francisco. The logo is team IP and needs NBA/team approval.

productHooks: A 'Go Dumb' Oakland-heritage capsule (shooting shirt, hoodie, crew socks) with scraper-foil piping and stunna-shade graphics. Co-design it with Vallejo and Oakland artists such as LaRussell, launch it at a Fox Theater show, and send proceeds to an East Oakland youth music or bike program.

Numbered Fillmore-style poster tees for marquee nights (Oct 21 at the Lakers, Dec 25 vs. Denver). Each is drawn by a commissioned Bay poster artist and sold with a printed poster at Amoeba Haight and the Chase Center team store.

A turntablism capsule for October's Filipino American History Month and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night, with scratch-waveform sleeves and slipmat hangtags. Co-create it with Bay Filipino-American DJs (approach DJ Qbert or P-Lo) and launch it with a Thrive City DJ set.
A DJ D-Sharp warmup tee for the home opener, with a QR code to a licensed D-Sharp Bay mix, sold at Thrive City.
A 'Roaracle' Town tee with a waveform of the 2007 We Believe crowd noise. Sell it in Oakland stores and at a Hiero Day or Oakland pop-up, not only at Chase Center.
watchouts: Brand conflicts: Stephen Curry ended his Under Armour partnership in late 2025 (Curry Brand is independent), and his next partner is unconfirmed. Use him only through NBA-licensed assets in music content. Check every artist's apparel and beverage deals (E-40's spirits businesses included) before approaching them.

Third-party IP needs licenses: Fillmore and Bill Graham archive posters, Grateful Dead marks (Steal Your Face, dancing bears), Hieroglyphics' third-eye logo, Thizz Entertainment marks and KMEL marks. So do all song titles, lyrics and audio. Commission new art instead of tracing classics.

Hyphy-era imagery carries drug and danger references ('thizz,' ghost-riding, sideshows), and Oakland is actively cracking down on sideshows. Keep product to music, dance, stunna shades and scraper bikes.
Oakland's loss is real: the Warriors, Raiders and A's all left. Oakland-nostalgia product without Oakland artists, Oakland launch venues and money back into Oakland will read as exploitation.

Filipino-American turntablism, Black Fillmore jazz history and Mission Latino music each belong to specific communities. Partner with them, credit them and pay them. Don't reduce any of them to a costume or a single stereotype.

Check whether Hiero Day ran in Oakland on Labor Day 2026, and its 2027 plans.
Check 2026-27 festival dates: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass (early October 2026), Carnaval SF, Stern Grove, Fillmore Jazz Festival, Outside Lands and San Jose Jazz Summer Fest 2027.
Confirm the Fillmore still gives free posters at sold-out shows, and find out who currently licenses the Bill Graham poster archive.

art.headline: Mission walls and Oakland posters drew the Bay's look long before the logo did.
art.summary: Bay art is collaborative and political. Mission murals, Oakland's Panther-era print graphics, San Francisco's poster lettering and a candy-paint car culture that runs south to San Jose give the team plenty to draw on. Many of those walls push back at the tech money now sitting courtside. Since the 2019 move, every cue has to say which side of the bridge it serves.

insights.title: The logo already picked the bridge
insights.detail: Since 2010 the Warriors' roundel has shown the Bay Bridge, which joins The City to The Town. The Golden Gate is the tourist bridge, and it leads to Marin. The team played 47 seasons in Oakland (1971-2019, minus 1996-97 in San Jose) before moving to Chase Center.
insights.implication: Make Bay Bridge cable lines and paired City/Town graphics the spine of any Warriors art program. Use Golden Gate orange as an accent at most. Give Oakland equal billing and equal commissions.

insights.title: The Town lost its teams but kept its look
insights.detail: Oakland lost the Warriors (2019), the Raiders (2020) and the A's (after 2024). Its civic identity now lives in Oaklandish's oak-tree tees, Uptown and KONO murals, and First Fridays on Telegraph Avenue.
insights.implication: Co-author Oakland-facing product with Oakland artists and sell it through Oakland doors. A 'The Town' graphic with no Oakland maker's name on it reads as the team cashing in on a place it left.

insights.title: Mission murals are community property with a point of view
insights.detail: Balmy Alley's garage-door murals, Precita Eyes' youth and tour programs, the Women's Building's MaestraPeace (1994) and Clarion Alley's rotating walls are all collectively made. Together they make the Mission one of America's densest mural districts. Clarion's recent work often targets tech-driven displacement, the same money that sits courtside at Chase Center.
insights.implication: Commission and pay Mission muralists through Precita Eyes. Never use the walls as a campaign backdrop, and never print photographed murals: they're the artists' copyright.

insights.title: San Francisco exported its own letterforms
insights.detail: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters invented the swelling, shape-filling psychedelic letter, and the Fillmore still hands posters to fans at sold-out shows. Walter Landor's 1975 continuous-line Muni worm and the sign-painter lettering of Margaret Kilgallen and Barry McGee are just as local.
insights.implication: Draw Warriors wordmarks in these traditions, as originals from living Bay letterers and poster artists, not stock script. License the Muni worm from SFMTA if it appears.

insights.title: Oakland is a print-and-poster city
insights.detail: Emory Douglas's graphics for The Black Panther newspaper use bold outlines, flat color and woodcut hatching. With Favianna Rodriguez's screenprints and Creative Growth's studio of artists with disabilities (since 1974), they make Oakland's art political, graphic and print-native.
insights.implication: Build February and community product on screenprint texture and Oakland printmakers, with credit and pay. Creative Growth is a strong candidate for an inclusive, artist-credited capsule.

insights.title: Car culture is the shared East Bay and South Bay language
insights.detail: Oakland's 'scrapers' are big-rim GM sedans in candy paint. East Oakland's Scraper Bike Team wraps its spokes in foil. San Jose's lowrider scene, where Lowrider Magazine was founded in 1977, shares the candy paint, metal flake and pinstriping.
insights.implication: Candy-paint finishes and pinstripe details can link Oakland and San Jose fans in one capsule made with named builders. Celebrate the craft, never the illegal sideshows.

insights.title: The arena's neighbors are galleries
insights.detail: Chase Center in Mission Bay sits a short walk from Dogpatch's Minnesota Street Project (2016) and ICA San Francisco (2022). Studios in the Bayview and Hunters Point Shipyard lie just beyond.
insights.implication: Stage artist reveals and limited art drops in Dogpatch on game nights, so the art program lives in the arena's own neighborhood and not only inside the team store.

places.name: Balmy Alley
places.neighborhood: Mission (24th to 25th St, between Treat Ave and Harrison St)
places.why: Murals since the early 1970s, including the 1984 PLACA project on Central America, make this the root of the Mission's community mural tradition.

places.name: Precita Eyes Mural Arts & Visitors Center
places.why: Susan Kelk Cervantes and Luis Cervantes founded it in 1977. It runs mural tours and youth programs, and it's the most credible door to commissioning Mission muralists.

places.name: Clarion Alley Mural Project
places.neighborhood: Mission (between Mission and Valencia, 17th and 18th Streets)
places.why: A rotating, artist-curated alley since 1992, with murals on housing, policing and tech displacement. It shows what the Mission is saying right now.

places.name: Minnesota Street Project
places.why: Opened in 2016 as a cluster of galleries and artist studios a short walk south of Chase Center. ICA San Francisco (2022) is on the same street.

places.name: African American Art & Culture Complex
places.why: The long-running home for Black visual and performing artists in a neighborhood once called the Harlem of the West, and a natural partner for San Francisco Black History product.

places.name: The Fillmore
places.neighborhood: Western Addition (Geary Blvd at Fillmore St)
places.why: Its hallways of concert posters and its poster handout at sold-out shows keep San Francisco's psychedelic lettering tradition alive.

places.name: Oakland Museum of California
places.why: Oakland's civic museum of California art and history, with major shows on the Black Panthers and on Bay Area art and design.

places.name: Creative Growth Art Center
places.kind: art studio and gallery for artists with disabilities
places.why: A working studio and gallery for artists with disabilities since 1974, and a model for credited, paid and inclusive collaboration.

places.name: MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana)
places.neighborhood: SoFA District, downtown San Jose (S. First St)
places.why: San Jose's main Latino contemporary art space, and the right door to South Bay Chicano and lowrider-rooted artists.

places.name: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco
places.why: It runs contemporary exhibitions and Chinatown art programs. Go here to find Chinese American artists for Lunar New Year work instead of using stock Chinatown imagery.

people.name: Emory Douglas
people.role: Graphic artist; Minister of Culture of the Black Panther Party
people.why: A San Francisco-raised artist whose Black Panther newspaper graphics defined Oakland's political visual language. A commission or tribute made with him carries real weight in The Town.

people.name: Precita Eyes Muralists (Susan Kelk Cervantes)
people.role: Mural collective and nonprofit; Cervantes is founder and a MaestraPeace co-painter
people.why: It has trained and organized generations of Mission muralists, and it's the community-accountable way to commission murals or mural-based product.

people.name: Barry McGee
people.role: Painter and graffiti writer (Twist); Mission School
people.why: The best-known figure in San Francisco's street-to-gallery lineage, with deep skateboard and streetwear credibility. A top-tier collaborator who needs a top-tier brief.

people.name: Favianna Rodriguez
people.role: Oakland-born printmaker and cultural organizer (Center for Cultural Power)
people.why: Her bold screenprints, including the 'Migration Is Beautiful' monarch, make her Oakland's best-known Latina graphic voice and a credible partner for Latino heritage product.

people.name: Jeremy Fish
people.why: His San Francisco-centric drawings have run through skate and streetwear graphics for two decades, including with Haight Street's Upper Playground. He's a natural fit for a City-side capsule.

people.name: Scraper Bike Team (Tyrone 'Baybe Champ' Stevenson Jr.)
people.why: They turned Oakland's scraper car style into candy-colored, foil-spoked bikes and a youth program. The best partner for a car-culture capsule.

people.name: Oaklandish
people.why: It started in 2000 as a public art project and became The Town's civic uniform. The benchmark for Oakland-pride product, and a possible partner.

people.name: FTC Skateboarding
people.why: Its multiple Nike SB Dunk collaborations make it San Francisco's most direct sneaker-culture link to Nike.

moments.name: FOG Design+Art
moments.why: The fair that benefits SFMOMA draws the city's collectors and design crowd, the same audience as Chase Center's premium seats. Reveal a high-end artist collaboration here.

moments.name: San Francisco Chinese New Year Festival & Parade
moments.timing: Lunar New Year is Feb 6, 2027 (Year of the Goat); the Chinatown night parade usually follows within about two weeks
moments.why: One of the largest Lunar New Year parades outside Asia, led by its long golden dragon, and the anchor for the Warriors' big Chinese American and Asian American fan base.

moments.name: Black Joy Parade
moments.why: Oakland's homegrown Black History Month celebration of color, costume and joy, and the right stage for Oakland Black artists' product.

moments.name: Oakland First Fridays
moments.timing: First Friday of every month, Telegraph Ave (KONO)
moments.why: The Town's monthly street festival of artists and vendors, which grew out of the Art Murmur gallery walks. A standing place to scout and launch Oakland work.

moments.name: Fillmore sold-out show poster handout
moments.why: The ritual that keeps San Francisco poster art collectible, and a ready model for numbered game-night prints.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's biggest costume and parade design moment, held during the 2027 playoff window.

moments.name: San Francisco Open Studios (ArtSpan)
moments.timing: Weekends from mid-October into November, neighborhood by neighborhood
moments.why: A citywide open-studios circuit that has run for decades and lines up with tip-off. It's the most efficient way to scout and sign City-side collaborators.

moments.name: Día de los Muertos procession and Festival of Altars
moments.timing: Nov 2 at dusk, Mission (altars in Garfield Square)
moments.why: A living community ritual since the early 1980s, where Mission artists build altars. Come to meet and listen to artists, not to sell merchandise.

vocabulary.meaning: Oakland, said with pride. Past Warriors uniforms have used it as an Oakland tribute.
San Francisco, and the wordmark on the 1960s San Francisco Warriors jersey. Locals never call it 'Frisco' or 'San Fran'.
Bay Area rap's name for the whole region, and a credible alternative to 'The Bay' on graphics.
The Bay-born intensifier ('hella cold'). It's the real thing but now a souvenir-shop staple, so use it sparingly and only in a local artist's hand.
Warriors fandom. 'The Dubs' is the team's everyday nickname.
Oakland and East Bay term for a 1970s-80s GM sedan on big rims in candy paint, and the root of East Oakland's scraper bikes.
The 1990s San Francisco art movement of Barry McGee, Margaret Kilgallen, Chris Johanson and Alicia McCarthy, built on graffiti, folk art and hand-painted signs.
Locals' nickname for San Francisco's summer fog, which has its own social-media persona. Shorthand for the city's cold, gray weather.

designCues.cue: Bay Bridge cable geometry: the suspension span's long catenaries and vertical hangers, with a dot-matrix run of white light points down the cables.
designCues.source: The Bay Bridge in the Warriors' logo since 2010, and Leo Villareal's The Bay Lights (2013) on the West Span's cables.
designCues.use: Catenary line graphics on side panels and shorts, with reflective dot-matrix prints. Any direct Bay Lights reference needs a license from the artist and Illuminate.

designCues.cue: Candy royal: Warriors royal #1D428A laid over silver metal flake as a candy-paint finish, with Warriors gold #FFC72C hand pinstriping.
designCues.source: Oakland scrapers, East Oakland's foil-spoked scraper bikes and San Jose lowriders.
designCues.use: Metal-flake prints, high-gloss trims and pinstripe details, co-designed with named Bay car-culture builders who get credit.

designCues.cue: Fillmore poster lettering: letters that swell and bend to fill a shape, in vibrating complementary color pairs.
designCues.source: Wes Wilson's 1966-67 Fillmore posters, which drew on Vienna Secession lettering, and the Bay's living gig-poster scene.
designCues.use: Commission a living Bay poster artist to draw an original 'DUBS' or 'THE CITY' lockup. Never trace Wilson, Victor Moscoso or Grateful Dead artwork.

designCues.cue: Two-city deco: tall, narrow Art Deco capitals stacked vertically like theater blade signs, with a neon edge glow.
designCues.source: Timothy Pflueger's Castro Theatre (San Francisco, 1922) and Paramount Theatre (Oakland, 1931), plus the Fox Oakland and Grand Lake marquees.
designCues.use: Stack 'THE CITY' and 'THE TOWN' down opposite side seams of one garment. Have a local sign painter draw an original alphabet instead of copying any one sign.

designCues.cue: Panther-press graphics: heavy black outlines, flat color fields and woodcut-style hatching, with people drawn at heroic scale.
designCues.source: Emory Douglas's art for The Black Panther newspaper, published in Oakland from 1967.
designCues.use: Screenprint-textured February product commissioned from Douglas or Oakland printmakers. No weapons, no 'pig' caricatures, and no reuse of archival Panther art without the artist and rights holders.

designCues.cue: Karl gray: the cool, slightly blue gray of fog pouring over Twin Peaks (approx. #C4C8CA).
designCues.source: San Francisco's summer fog, nicknamed Karl, which makes layering the local uniform.
designCues.use: A heather base for fleece and layering pieces, with Warriors gold as the only accent. A quiet City-side alternative to Golden Gate orange.

designCues.cue: Alley panel quilt: one garment built from separately authored panels, each a different muralist's story, like Balmy Alley's garage doors.
designCues.source: Balmy Alley, painted since the early 1970s, including the 1984 PLACA project.
designCues.use: A multi-artist warm-up jacket or shooting shirt with each panel credited on the jock tag, commissioned through Precita Eyes. Never print photographs of existing murals.

designCues.cue: Necklace of Lights: a scalloped string of round bulbs looping the water and doubled in its reflection.
designCues.source: Lake Merritt's lights, first strung in 1925 and later restored, around the lake where Oakland gathers.
designCues.use: A scalloped bulb-chain trim or all-over print for Oakland-facing product, sold through Oakland shops.

productHooks: 'The City / The Town' capsule: fog-gray heather base, Bay Bridge catenary graphics, and Pflueger-style blade lettering with 'THE CITY' down one seam and 'THE TOWN' down the other. One San Francisco letterer and one Oakland letterer draw it, and both are credited and paid.

'Candy Paint' capsule: Warriors royal over metal flake with gold pinstriping and reflective foil-spoke trims. Co-design it with the Scraper Bike Team and San Jose lowrider builders, and launch it in East Oakland and at MACLA.
Numbered game-night posters: a Bay poster artist draws a Fillmore-style screenprint for select marquee home games. Hand it to fans, sell it with a matching tee, and have the artist sign the run.

Oakland Black History capsule for February, timed to the Black Joy Parade: screenprint graphics from Emory Douglas or Oakland printmakers, sold through Oaklandish and Black-owned Oakland shops. Proceeds go to an Oakland organization the artist chooses.
Mission panel jacket for the Warriors' Latino heritage night or Carnaval weekend. A Precita Eyes muralist paints each panel and is credited on the jock tag.

Lunar New Year 2027 (Year of the Goat) capsule drawn by Chinatown-rooted artists found through the Chinese Culture Center. Use neon blade-sign characters by a local calligrapher, not 'chop suey' type.
watchouts: Third-party IP is everywhere. The Golden Gate Bridge district licenses the bridge's name and image, The Bay Lights is Leo Villareal's artwork, the Muni worm belongs to SFMTA, and Oaklandish owns its tree logo. Grateful Dead and classic Fillmore poster art need licenses. Murals are protected by copyright and California's Art Preservation Act.

Oakland is still sore about the 2019 move, and it lost the Raiders and A's too. Oakland cues need Oakland artists, Oakland retail and visible credit, or they read as nostalgia merch from the team that left.
Clarion Alley and many Mission murals protest tech-driven displacement. A brand shoot against them would be tone-deaf, so go through Precita Eyes and the artists themselves.

Avoid caricature. No 'chop suey' fonts or generic dragons for Chinatown. No Panther guns. No sugar-skull merchandise from Día de los Muertos. No Old English or placa lettering lifted from Chicano street culture without Chicano artists. Celebrate scrapers and lowriders, never sideshows.

Stephen Curry ended his Under Armour partnership in late 2025 (Curry Brand is now independent) and is reportedly a sneaker free agent. Confirm his current footwear and apparel deal before commissioning any artist portrait of him for Nike product. Lean on team and city art rather than player likeness.

verify: Check the Warriors' City Edition history (including past Oakland 'The Town' tributes) and what the 2026-27 City Edition and Specter uniforms use, so these concepts don't duplicate them.
Confirm Stephen Curry's current footwear and apparel deal (he left Under Armour in late 2025; a new partner is unconfirmed) before any portrait-based product.
Check dates for the Warriors' 2026-27 Lunar New Year, Black History and Latino heritage nights. Check the 2027 San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade too (Lunar New Year is Feb 6, 2027).
Confirm the Black Joy Parade 2027 date and Oakland First Fridays' current schedule and format on Telegraph Ave.
Check San Francisco Open Studios 2026 weekends (ArtSpan) and FOG Design+Art January 2027 dates.
Confirm Carnaval San Francisco 2027 dates (expected Memorial Day weekend, May 29-30).
Confirm FTC Skateboarding, Upper Playground and Oaklandish are still operating, and where their stores are.
Check the Scraper Bike Team's current activity and leadership.
Check whether The Bay Lights is currently lit (the original installation went dark in 2023) and who licenses it.
Check current Golden Gate Bridge district licensing rules for the bridge's name and image, and SFMTA licensing for the Muni worm.
Check Clarion Alley's current murals and CAMP's position on commercial photo shoots.
Confirm the Fillmore still hands out commemorative posters at sold-out shows.

food.headline: Chase Center sits where the Bay's food lines cross, and the season runs through crab.
food.summary: Bay food passes any swap test: sourdough with a bacterium named for San Francisco, the foil-wrapped Mission burrito, Dungeness crab at Christmas. Its living edge is immigrant and community kitchens, from Chinatown and Daly City to Fruitvale's taco trucks and Black-owned Oakland barbecue. Take cues from the table, make them with the businesses that own it, and sell in Oakland as well as at Chase Center.

insights.title: Chase Center sits on a food line
insights.detail: The Central Subway opened in late 2022. Since then the T Third light rail has run from Chinatown–Rose Pak station past the UCSF/Chase Center stop, then down Third Street into Bayview, the city's historically Black neighborhood. 16th Street runs from the arena door straight west to the Mission's taquerías. Thrive City, the plaza wrapped around the arena, is the pregame meeting point and the road-game watch-party site.
insights.implication: Plan game-day launches as a route, not a booth. Pay one Chinatown bakery and one Bayview kitchen for collab menu items, and drop product at Thrive City and at both ends of the line.

insights.title: Christmas night is crab night
insights.detail: Dungeness crab is the Bay's holiday meal. The commercial season traditionally opens in mid-November, though recent openers have been delayed by whale-entanglement and domoic-acid rules. Christmas Eve means cioppino, the stew North Beach's Ligurian fishermen created. From January to March, 'crab feeds' (all-you-can-eat fundraisers) fill parish halls and school gyms. The Warriors host Denver on Christmas night at 7:30 p.m. PT.
insights.implication: A Christmas-game holiday pack in cooked-crab orange on Warriors navy is pure Bay. Tie part of the proceeds to a community crab feed, and don't date-lock product to the crab opener.

insights.title: Bread is the Bay's texture library
insights.detail: Sourdough's signature bacterium was named Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis for the city in 1971. Boudin traces its mother dough to 1849, and Tartine's scored country loaf set the modern standard. Dutch crunch, the crackle-topped roll, is the default sandwich bread at Bay delis and almost unknown outside Northern California.
insights.implication: No other market owns Dutch crunch crackle or sourdough scoring. Use them as tonal embosses, jacquards or prints on warm-ups, with the bacterium story on an inside label.

insights.title: Oakland feeds the loyalty
insights.detail: Oakland, the team's home from 1971 to 2019, has its own table. There's Everett & Jones Barbeque (Black-owned since 1973), the taco trucks along International Boulevard through Fruitvale, Oakland Chinatown, and Ethiopian and Eritrean kitchens on Telegraph. Chefs include Tanya Holland, Nelson German and Reem Assil. Many Oakland fans still cheer the team and still resent the move across the bay.
insights.implication: Give Oakland a drop of its own, co-created with Oakland food businesses and sold in Oakland, not a nostalgia graphic sold at Chase Center.

insights.title: Filipino, Vietnamese and Chinese kitchens are the fan base's comfort food
insights.detail: Daly City is roughly a third Filipino, and Mitchell's Ice Cream has served ube and buko since long before ube went national. San Jose has the largest Vietnamese population of any U.S. city, and Lee's Sandwiches was founded there in 1983. The An family's garlic noodles at Thanh Long, served since 1971, became a citywide classic. October is Filipino American History Month, and the Warriors hold an annual Filipino Heritage Night.
insights.implication: Heritage capsules (ube for Filipino Heritage Night, Lunar New Year and Tết in February) should be co-designed with Filipino-, Vietnamese- and Chinese-American Bay creatives and kitchens. Credit and pay them. Don't build from color swatches.

insights.title: The Mission burrito is the city's edible logo, and a displacement flashpoint
insights.detail: The foil-wrapped Mission-style burrito is San Francisco's most recognizable dish. La Taqueria famously leaves out the rice. FiveThirtyEight named it America's best burrito in 2014, and it's a James Beard America's Classic. The 24th Street corridor became the Calle 24 Latino Cultural District in 2014 to protect Latino businesses from tech-boom displacement. La Cocina in the Mission incubates immigrant women food entrepreneurs.
insights.implication: Burrito foil and hand-painted taquería lettering work only when Latino businesses and artists are paid partners. Go through Calle 24 or La Cocina, and never frame the burrito as tech-worker fuel.

insights.title: The Currys made food part of the franchise's face
insights.detail: Ayesha Curry built a food brand: the cookbooks The Seasoned Life and The Full Plate, Food Network's Ayesha's Home Kitchen, and Sweet July. She and Stephen run the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation, which funds child nutrition and food access in Oakland. Stephen launched Gentleman's Cut bourbon, and Jimmy Butler owns Bigface Coffee.
insights.implication: A food-access night with Eat. Learn. Play. fits Dub Nation. But athlete ventures are separate IP bound up with endorsement deals. Check Curry's and Butler's current footwear and apparel contracts, and keep alcohol off youth product.

places.name: Thrive City
places.why: The plaza wrapped around Chase Center is the pregame meeting point and has hosted official watch parties for road playoff games. It's the obvious place for food-collab pop-ups.

places.name: La Taqueria
places.why: It serves the canonical Mission burrito, with no rice and an optional 'dorado' crisped tortilla. Every burrito argument in the city starts here.

places.name: Thanh Long
places.why: The An family's roast Dungeness crab and garlic noodles, served since 1971, are the Bay's Vietnamese-American special-occasion meal.

places.name: Swan Oyster Depot
places.why: Open since 1912, this counter-only seafood bar sums up the city's crab culture, with its line for Dungeness crab, oysters and 'crab back'.

places.name: Mister Jiu's
places.why: Brandon Jew's Michelin-starred Chinese-American restaurant on Waverly Place is a short walk from the T line's Chinatown–Rose Pak terminus.

places.name: Old Skool Cafe
places.why: A jazz-era supper club in Bayview, staffed by young people coming out of the justice and foster-care systems.

places.name: Everett & Jones Barbeque
places.why: Dorothy Everett and her family opened it in 1973. It's Oakland's Black-owned barbecue standard and an Oakland-first partner.

places.name: International Boulevard taco trucks
places.why: The Bay's densest run of taco trucks, panaderías and mariscos stands, and the everyday food of Oakland's Mexican and Central American community.

places.name: Mitchell's Ice Cream
places.why: Open since 1953 and famous for Filipino and tropical flavors (ube, buko, macapuno) that families drive in for from Daly City to Vallejo.

places.name: La Victoria Taqueria
places.why: Its cult orange sauce, sold by the bottle, is San Jose's edible signature and a late-night SJSU rite.

people.name: Ayesha Curry
people.role: Cookbook author, TV host, founder of Sweet July, co-founder with Stephen Curry of the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation
people.why: The Bay food figure most closely tied to the team. Eat. Learn. Play.'s Oakland food-access work makes a credible, non-commercial partner for a Nike food night.

people.name: Alice Waters
people.role: Founder of Chez Panisse (Berkeley, 1971) and the Edible Schoolyard
people.why: She defined 'California cuisine' (seasonal, local, farmers-market first), the Bay's food self-image that every chef here still answers to.

people.name: Brandon Jew
people.role: Chef-owner of Mister Jiu's; author of Mister Jiu's in Chinatown
people.why: The leading voice for modern Chinese-American cooking at the Chinatown end of the T line, and a natural Lunar New Year partner.

people.name: Tanya Holland
people.role: Oakland chef, founder of Brown Sugar Kitchen, author of Tanya Holland's California Soul
people.why: Oakland's most prominent Black culinary voice, with a national platform through Top Chef and the James Beard Foundation.

people.name: Nelson German
people.role: Dominican-American Oakland chef (alaMar, Sobre Mesa; confirm both still operate); Top Chef contestant
people.why: His Afro-Latino Oakland cooking pairs naturally with Dominican-born Al Horford for a heritage collab.

people.name: Reem Assil
people.role: Palestinian-Syrian-American chef, founder of Reem's California, author of Arabiyya
people.why: She built an Arab street bakery in Oakland's Fruitvale around worker-centered values, and she's a leading voice in the East Bay's immigrant food scene.

people.name: La Cocina
people.role: Mission District nonprofit incubator for low-income, mostly immigrant women food entrepreneurs (founded 2005)
people.why: The most credible pipeline to paid, credited collabs with immigrant-owned food businesses.

people.name: Señor Sisig
people.role: Filipino-Mexican food truck and restaurant brand founded in 2010 by Evan Kidera and Gil Payumo
people.why: Its sisig burritos and merch are Bay Filipino-American pride, which makes it a natural Filipino Heritage Night partner.

moments.name: Tip-off meets Filipino American History Month
moments.why: Filipino American History Month lines up with the start of the season, and the Warriors' Filipino Heritage Night is the natural launch for an ube capsule.

moments.name: Dungeness crab season opener
moments.why: The Bay's food calendar turns on it, with crab back on menus from Swan Oyster Depot to Thanh Long.

moments.name: Christmas night: Nuggets at Warriors
moments.why: The national nightcap comes from Chase Center the day after the Bay's Christmas Eve cioppino-and-crab tradition.

moments.name: Crab feed season
moments.why: All-you-can-eat Dungeness fundraisers run by schools, parishes and clubs are the Bay's most local winter ritual.

moments.name: Lunar New Year and Tết
moments.timing: Feb 6, 2027; SF Chinatown parade and San Jose Tết events follow
moments.why: San Francisco's Chinese New Year Parade is one of the largest outside Asia, and San Jose's Vietnamese community celebrates Tết on the same date.

moments.name: Black Joy Parade
moments.why: This Black History Month celebration brings Black-owned food vendors to downtown Oakland.

moments.name: Carnaval San Francisco
moments.why: The Mission's street festival of Latino and Caribbean food and music falls in the conference-finals window.

moments.name: Pregame at Thrive City
moments.why: Fans gather on the arena plaza before tip-off, and return for watch parties during road playoff runs.

vocabulary.meaning: A Mission-style burrito 'super'-sized with cheese, sour cream and guacamole. Locals order it 'super' by default.
The crackle-topped sandwich roll, standard at Bay delis and rare elsewhere. 'On Dutch crunch' is the local order.
An all-you-can-eat Dungeness crab fundraiser dinner held by schools, parishes and clubs in winter.
The Bay's word for bubble tea. A 'boba run' is a social ritual, especially for Asian-American youth.
Butter-and-garlic noodles popularized by Thanh Long, now on menus across the Bay and usually ordered with roast crab.
The Town is Oakland and The City is San Francisco. Call an Oakland food drop 'The City' and it fails.
A scramble of ground beef, spinach, onion and egg, a staple of the city's Italian-American 'Joe's' restaurants, including Original Joe's in North Beach and San Jose.
A sourdough starter kept alive for years. Boudin says its mother dough dates to 1849.

designCues.cue: Cooked Dungeness orange: the brick-orange of a boiled crab shell, paired with its shell-cream underside (#F3E3C3) on Warriors navy #1D428A
designCues.source: Dungeness crab season, Christmas Eve cioppino and winter crab feeds
designCues.use: Use it as a holiday-pack accent on collar tipping, number outlines and a bib-shaped hangtag. Leave off restaurant marks.

designCues.cue: Ube halaya purple, the deep violet of Filipino purple-yam jam, set against Warriors gold #FFC72C
designCues.source: Filipino-American desserts, from Daly City bakeries to Mitchell's ube ice cream
designCues.use: Use it for the Filipino Heritage Night colorway, co-designed with Filipino-American Bay designers. Keep the Philippine flag's sun and stars off unless partners lead.

designCues.cue: Dutch crunch crackle: the irregular cracked-plate pattern of the rice-paste topping, browned darker at the seams
designCues.source: The default sandwich roll at Bay delis
designCues.use: Use it as a tonal emboss on gold fleece or a jacquard on warm-up sleeves. No other market can claim the texture.

designCues.cue: 'Named for the city': Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis, the sourdough bacterium, plus a single curved scoring 'ear' and a flour-dust bloom
designCues.source: San Francisco sourdough (Boudin since 1849, Tartine's country loaf)
designCues.use: Put a tonal scoring-slash graphic on the back yoke and the bacterium story on the inside label. It's science, not a trademark.

designCues.cue: Crinkled burrito foil: mirror-silver foil with soft hand-folded creases
designCues.source: Mission taquerías' foil-wrapped burritos
designCues.use: Use foil-print packaging and hangtags, or reflective crinkle trim, on a limited Mission drop made with Calle 24 or La Cocina partners.

designCues.cue: Hand-painted storefront lettering: brush script and drop-shadow block letters in red, green and yellow
designCues.source: Taquería, panadería and produce-market signs on Mission Street, 24th Street and International Boulevard
designCues.use: Commission working Bay sign painters to letter names and numbers for Mission or Fruitvale drops. Credit and pay them.

designCues.cue: La Vic's orange sauce: the bright, creamy chili-orange of San Jose's cult taquería sauce
designCues.source: La Victoria Taqueria, downtown San Jose
designCues.use: Use it as a South Bay accent on navy for a San Jose drop. Use the name or bottle only under license from La Victoria.

designCues.cue: T Third route line: a single line from Chinatown–Rose Pak through Chase Center to Bayview, with food-stop dots
designCues.source: Muni's T Third line and the Central Subway
designCues.use: Draw an original route-map graphic for shooting shirts and tees. Don't use the Muni 'worm' logo or SFMTA marks without a license.

productHooks: T Line Table capsule: a shooting shirt and tee with an original route graphic from Chinatown–Rose Pak through Chase Center to Bayview's Third Street. Launch it with paid collab menu items from a Chinatown bakery and a Bayview kitchen, and run it from Lunar New Year (Feb 6, 2027) through Black History Month.

Crab Feed holiday pack for the Dec 25 game against Denver: a navy fleece with cooked-crab orange (#D4502A) and shell-cream accents, a bib-shaped hangtag and butcher-paper-print packaging. Part of the proceeds funds a community crab feed through Eat. Learn. Play. or an Oakland or Bayview nonprofit.
Dutch Crunch pregame hoodie: a crackle emboss on Warriors gold (#FFC72C), a sourdough-scoring tonal back graphic and the 'named for the city' bacterium story on the inside label.
Ube and gold Filipino Heritage Night capsule for October, co-designed with Filipino-American Bay artists. Add a Señor Sisig pop-up at Thrive City and retail in Daly City and Vallejo.
Town Table Oakland drop: released only at a Lake Merritt or Fruitvale pop-up, co-created with Everett & Jones and International Boulevard truck owners, and lettered by Oakland sign painters.
Foil Pack regional tees: a Mission version in crinkle-foil packaging made with Calle 24 and La Cocina chefs, and a San Jose version with a licensed La Vic's orange accent.
watchouts: Every business named here (La Taqueria, La Victoria, Mitchell's, Thanh Long, Boudin, Señor Sisig) owns its name and look. License, credit and pay it. Don't use Muni's 'worm' logo or other SFMTA marks without permission.

The Mission and Bayview have lived through tech-era displacement, and the move to a pricier San Francisco arena is part of that story. Partner through community groups (Calle 24, La Cocina, Bayview organizations) and price for access. Keep Día de los Muertos altar and procession imagery off product.
Oakland still hurts from the 2019 move. Make Oakland product with Oakland businesses and sell it in Oakland, not as a nostalgia graphic at Chase Center.

Athlete food ventures (Ayesha Curry's brands, Gentleman's Cut bourbon, Butler's Bigface Coffee) are separate IP tied to endorsement deals. Confirm Stephen Curry's and Jimmy Butler's current footwear and apparel partners, and keep alcohol references off youth product.
Bay restaurants open and close quickly, and the Dungeness opener moves from year to year. Reconfirm every partner before committing, and never date-lock product to the crab season.

Confirm Stephen Curry's current footwear and apparel partner (he ended his Under Armour deal in late 2025; new partner unconfirmed) and Jimmy Butler's current shoe deal, before any athlete-linked food collab.
Check dates and formats of the Warriors' 2026-27 Filipino Heritage Night, Lunar New Year night and Black History Month games.
Confirm the opening date of the 2026-27 Dungeness crab commercial season for the San Francisco area (recent openers have been delayed).
Check whether the 2026-27 City Edition or the Warriors' Specter uniforms already use Chinatown, Lunar New Year or food references, so a capsule doesn't repeat them.
Lunar New Year 2027 falls on Feb 6. Confirm the dates of the 2027 San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade and San Jose Tết festival.
Confirm the T Third still runs from Chinatown–Rose Pak to Bayview via the UCSF/Chase Center stop (SFMTA has adjusted service patterns since 2023).
Confirm Old Skool Cafe (Bayview) is still operating, and which Everett & Jones Barbeque locations in Oakland are open.
